songs.about: The Edge of Life follows someone caught between life and death, watching their whole life pass before their eyes as something pulls them through the veil. On the other side the pain is gone, but they are torn between a body that wants to stay and a soul that wants to move on. In the end, the song suggests that the legacy we leave behind is what really matters.

Firstly My Breakfast is told by someone who never cared, turning a single shared night into a cold rejection of the other person's love. It exposes what it feels like to be used and thrown away, and borrows a passage from Arthur Rimbaud's A Season in Hell, where a swallowed poison burns from the inside.

Tide of Fears is about feeling out of place in a world ruled by old rules carved in stone. It questions people who do good only out of fear of punishment or hope of reward, and argues for thinking for yourself and staying true to your own values, even when doubt pulls you under.

Buried Thoughts was inspired by the film Hannibal and is narrated by Mason Verger, the disfigured victim who spends years planning his revenge on Hannibal Lecter. Behind the story are the hidden wounds that bullying can leave long after the fact, and a message to reach out for help instead of carrying them alone.

Fallen Dreams was inspired by the film Vanilla Sky. It is about falling from the top, when ego and stubbornness bring down everything you had built and the dream turns into a fall with no end. Even with broken wings, the song refuses to give up and promises to climb back up and rise again.

Change is a motivational song that puts the listener in front of the mirror and asks what they really see there: regrets, sorrow or answers. Its message is that only you can turn your own life around, so believe in yourself and don't let the chance to change pass you by.

Today is Sunday is about a daily routine so driven by work that it swallows personal life. It captures the panic of waking up on a Sunday convinced it is a workday and that you are late again, until you remember what day it is and go back to sleep. The song plays it for laughs, but the pressure behind the joke is real.

Faithless Breath looks at belief held without conviction, and at the hypocrisy of those who turn other people's beliefs into a business. It questions leaders who move others like puppets, while recognising that people need something to hold on to and a reason to carry on.

Make Decisions is a call to break the chains that hold you back and take control of your own life. It reminds the listener that every action shapes the path ahead, and that it is never too late to change your mind and stop picking up the pieces of the past.

Tears of Blood is about a forbidden love, a passion for someone you know you have to resist. Far away and heartbroken, the narrator cannot put the feelings into words and wonders whether running from love is the answer, wishing only to wake up from the pain.

Faceless Demons brings the metalcore side of Silicon Fortress to bear on cyberbullying and the anonymous haters who hide behind a screen. It speaks to anyone worn down by online abuse and the depression that can follow, and urges them to stand up to those voices instead of facing them alone.

Keep Away deals with depression and the fears that can knock you down without warning. The song argues for holding on to what makes you happy and stepping away from what hurts you. It was the ninth single from Silicon Fortress and the last one out before the album.

The title track compares the rise of technology, and of social networks above all, to a fortress built from silicon. It looks at people who act one way online and another in real life, hiding behind their screens until a healthy social life slips out of reach.

Age of Lies takes on fake news and a world run on appearances, where every bubble tells its own version of events. Over heavy riffs, it challenges the listener to question what they are told and work out what is actually true.

The band's namesake song is a call to be yourself, whatever society and social media say you should look like, wear or think. It doubles as an open invitation to join the Insane Family and enjoy the ride on your own terms.

Desperate Prayer puts a believer and an atheist side by side on a plane that is going down, sharing the same fate. As the end gets closer, the song asks whether one could lose his faith and the other find it, and hides a message about empathy for the listener to uncover.

Ghosts is about the people close to you, a friend or a partner, who slowly drain your energy and pull you down without you noticing. By the time you see them for what they are, they may have taken your dreams and joy with them, and the dependence is hard to break.

Inspired by Yuval Noah Harari's book Sapiens, Imagined Realities looks at the things humans invented and agreed to believe in, such as money, borders, laws and companies. Those shared fictions let us live together in huge numbers but have also led to war, and the song asks what part we play in that game.

Invisible Chains follows a relationship that starts out well until one partner begins to control the other. It shows how an abusive relationship turns into a nightmare and leaves deep scars. It was the eighth single from Silicon Fortress.

Distant Hearts is the ballad of Silicon Fortress, about loving someone who lives far away. It explores long-distance and online relationships and the challenges that come with them, and it was the album's fourth single.

The Sun Will Rise carries a hopeful message: whatever adversity comes, things will turn out okay. It starts out in the cold, fighting the demons inside, and turns into a call to let go of the darkness and let the light back in. Like the sun, the song says, we will rise again and find our way back to the path of life.

Waiting for You is a song about resilience, about refusing to break while time slips away. Its narrator stands in the shadows waiting for someone to arrive, holding on to a flicker of light through every trial. It ends sure that it is never too late.

releases.silicon-fortress: Silicon Fortress is Insane Driver's second album, released in 2021. Across eleven tracks of hard rock, heavy metal and metalcore, it looks at technology, social media and modern society, from cyberbullying and fake news to abusive and long-distance relationships. Nine of its songs came out as singles before the album.
releases.insane-driver: Insane Driver is the band's self-titled debut album, released in 2016. Its eleven tracks mix hard rock, heavy metal and metalcore, from the instrumental opener Endless Path to songs like The Edge of Life, Buried Thoughts and Today Is Sunday.
releases.insane-driver-deluxe: The 2018 deluxe edition of Insane Driver's 2016 debut album keeps all eleven original hard rock and heavy metal tracks. It adds deluxe versions of Firstly My Breakfast, Buried Thoughts and Today Is Sunday, plus an acoustic version of Tide of Fears.
releases.waiting-for-you: Waiting for You is a 2025 single by Insane Driver, the hard rock, heavy metal and metalcore band from São Paulo, Brazil. It came out on its own, outside any album.
releases.the-sun-will-rise: The Sun Will Rise is a 2024 hard rock and heavy metal single by Insane Driver. It carries a hopeful message: whatever challenges come, things will turn out okay.
releases.today-is-sunday-eder-franco: This 2017 version of Today Is Sunday is credited to Eder Franco, Insane Driver's lead vocalist. The song first appeared on the band's 2016 debut album.
releases.change-live: Change (Live) is a 2015 live recording of Change, performed at Acustica Studios, where the band also filmed the performance video. The studio version appeared a year later on the 2016 debut album Insane Driver.
releases.fallen-dreams-acoustic: Fallen Dreams (Acoustic) is a 2019 acoustic version of Fallen Dreams, the song inspired by the film Vanilla Sky from Insane Driver's 2016 debut album. In a stripped-back arrangement, it keeps the song's promise to rise again after a fall.
